result.title: Same Facts, Different Decision: Fact-Invariant Manipulation and Provenance-Based Defense in Typed Decision Models
result.summary: Typed decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer only with a probability, an option, or a score, so software can act on them directly. Their inputs, however, often include text from outsiders. Prior attacks test this risk poorly. Injected instructions rarely work on these models, and added facts can make a changed decision correct. We show that outside comments can persuade these models to make a wrong decision without adding any fact. We propose LEVER, an attack that writes such comments with four levers from argumentation theory, uses a separate verifier to discard any comment that adds a fact, and searches for effective comments guided by the model's output probabilities. We further propose the Provenance Gate, a defense that accepts a changed decision only if the model reaches it again without the outside comments. On three benchmarks, LEVER flips about a third of Jev's correct decisions, 2.8 times as many as the strongest prior attack under the same limit on facts, and more on five other models. The gate blocks all of these attacks with at most one extra query and still accepts trusted updates.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究类型化决策模型（如 Jev）在收到外部文本评论时，可在不新增事实的情况下被说服改变决策，提出基于论证理论四个杠杆的 LEVER 攻击，以及要求去掉外部评论后仍能复现同一决策的 Provenance Gate 防御。
AI.relevance_reason: 对象为非视觉的类型化决策模型，既无视觉证据筛选也无 latent 推理状态生成与更新，事实不变性与来源门控只涉及纯文本扰动和决策复现，与 LVR 的表示、生成或训练监督缺乏实质联系。
